function.description: Retrieves the weather forecast for a specified location and date range. The forecast includes temperature, precipitation, and wind speed. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location for which the weather forecast is requested, in the format of 'City, Country' (e.g., 'London, UK').

start_date.description: The start date of the period for the weather forecast in the ISO 8601 format (e.g., '2023-04-01').

end_date.description: The end date of the period for the weather forecast in the ISO 8601 format (e.g., '2023-04-07').

units.description: The unit system in which to return the weather forecast data.

include_details.description: Specifies whether to include detailed forecast information such as humidity and visibility.

**How Turbonomic Helps Unilever Leverage AI for Multi‑Cloud Observability**

| Goal | What Turbonomic Does | Why It Matters for Unilever |
|------|---------------------|-----------------------------|
| **Unified Visibility** | Aggregates real‑time telemetry from all workloads—VMs, containers, serverless functions, databases, etc.—across GCP, AWS, Azure, and on‑prem environments into a single dashboard. | Unilever can see the health, performance, and cost of every application component in one place, eliminating siloed monitoring. |
| **Predictive Capacity Planning** | Uses machine learning to forecast future resource demand (CPU, memory, I/O) based on historical usage patterns and upcoming business events (seasonal spikes, new product launches). | Enables proactive scaling decisions before performance degrades or costs spike. |
| **Automated Remediation** | Applies policy‑driven actions (right‑size, move, pause, terminate) automatically or recommends them to operators. | Reduces manual toil, speeds up response times, and ensures compliance with SLAs. |
| **Cost Optimization** | Continuously analyzes spend vs. utilization, identifies waste (idle instances, over‑provisioned resources), and suggests or executes cost‑saving moves (spot instances, rightsizing, reserved capacity). | Helps Unilever keep cloud budgets under control while maintaining performance. |
| **Business‑Driven Policies** | Lets Unilever encode business priorities (e.g., “Retail launch traffic must stay below X latency”) into policies that guide automated decisions. | Aligns IT operations directly with corporate objectives. |
| **Cross‑Cloud Workload Mobility** | Provides a consistent set of APIs and policy models that work across all clouds, making it easier to shift workloads for cost, performance, or regulatory reasons. | Gives Unilever flexibility to choose the best cloud for each workload without being locked into a single vendor’s ecosystem. |

---

### Difference Between Turbonomic and Native Cloud Monitoring/Optimization Tools

| Feature | Turbonomic | GCP Operations Suite (formerly Stackdriver) | AWS CloudWatch & Cost Explorer | Azure Monitor & Advisor |
|---------|------------|-------------------------------------------|--------------------------------|--------------------------|
| **Scope** | Unified across multiple clouds + on‑prem | Cloud‑specific (GCP only) | Cloud‑specific (AWS only) | Cloud‑specific (Azure only) |
| **Observability Layer** | Real‑time telemetry + AI‑based analytics | Metrics, logs, traces (native stack) | Metrics, logs, traces (native stack) | Metrics, logs, traces (native stack) |
| **AI / ML Capabilities** | Predictive capacity planning, anomaly detection, automated remediation | Basic anomaly alerts, no predictive modeling | Basic anomaly alerts, no predictive modeling | Basic anomaly alerts, no predictive modeling |
| **Automation** | Policy‑driven automation (move, resize, pause, terminate) | Limited automation via Cloud Functions / Lambda (requires custom code) | Limited automation via Lambda / Step Functions (requires custom code) | Limited automation via Logic Apps / Automation (requires custom code) |
| **Cost Optimization** | Continuous cost‑vs‑performance analysis, actionable recommendations, automated moves | Cost Explorer provides reports but no automated actions | Cost Explorer provides reports but no automated actions | Advisor provides recommendations but no automated actions |
| **Policy Management** | Central policy engine that applies consistently across all clouds | Policies are cloud‑specific (IAM, VPC, etc.) | Policies are cloud‑specific (IAM, Security Hub, etc.) | Policies are cloud‑specific (IAM, Security Center, etc.) |
| **Integration** | Works with Kubernetes, OpenShift, VMware vSphere, Hyper‑visor APIs, and cloud provider APIs | Native integration only within GCP services | Native integration only within AWS services | Native integration only within Azure services |
| **Operational Overhead** | One platform to learn, one set of dashboards, one set of alerts | Multiple dashboards per cloud, separate alerting systems | Multiple dashboards per cloud, separate alerting systems | Multiple dashboards per cloud, separate alerting systems |
| **Vendor Lock‑In Risk** | Low – independent of any single cloud vendor | High – tied to GCP | High – tied to AWS | High – tied to Azure |

#### Bottom Line

Turbonomic acts as a **single pane of glass** that brings together telemetry, AI analytics, and policy‑driven automation across all of Unilever’s cloud and on‑prem environments. Native tools from GCP, AWS, and Azure provide powerful monitoring and cost‑reporting capabilities, but they lack the cross‑cloud AI‑driven automation and unified policy engine that Turbonomic offers. By adopting Turbonomic, Unilever can:

* Reduce operational complexity and learning curves.
* Automate right‑size and migration decisions at scale.
* Align IT operations tightly with business goals.
* Keep cloud spend predictable while meeting performance SLAs.

This holistic approach is especially valuable for a global consumer goods company like Unilever, where workloads span multiple regions, regulatory regimes, and business units.
